item.title: A Practical Follow-up Program for Research and Policy
item.lead: The seven-part series can best be continued with a methodical research program in which each significant claim is given its own evidentiary path.

blocks.text: Step 1 is source inventory. Collect contracts, platform terms and conditions, internal manuals, CRM screenshots, technical logs, and relevant financial documents. Label each item by origin, date, and reliability.

Step 2 is reconstruction. For each case, construct a timeline that juxtaposes interaction, data storage, script usage, and payment. This reveals which components are factually interconnected and which are merely assumed.
Step 3 is comparison. Investigate multiple accounts, multiple agencies, and multiple jurisdictions so that a pattern is not based on a single anomaly.

Step 4 is independent verification. Have legal, technical, and sociological reviewers each assess their own component. This prevents one discipline from automatically accepting claims from another discipline as proven.

Step 5 is publication with uncertainty labels. A professional dossier can be both robust and cautious: it clarifies what is established, what is plausible, what remains a hypothesis, and what data is still missing.
